_source: captured from `git show origin/main:cloudbuild.yaml` at 0910192 (FC-081 merged). This fixture pins MAIN's deploy flags. FC-084 intentionally adds --revision-suffix on top of them; that exception is declared in ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS in tests/test_cloudbuild_contract.py. Regenerate only alongside a deliberate, reviewed deploy-flag change.
_deviations: One value here is deliberately NOT main's: `timeout` is 1500s, main is 1200s. FC-084 raises it because a build that waits for an older one needs ~1158s worst case (wait <=798s for the older build + its own ~360s deploy chain), which left only ~42s of headroom under 1200s. Both adversarial reviews called the original 1200s must-not-change a plan defect. serialize-builds' BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is asserted equal to this value by test_gate_deadline_tracks_the_build_timeout. SECOND DEVIATION (FC-060 Layer 3): `deploy-sweep-job` is added to `step_ids` (LAST, behind all three promotes) and `wait_for`, and `deploy-dashboard-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `SWEEP_JOB_NAME=backtest-sweep`. The env VALUE is part of the frozen flag string, so it cannot be absorbed by ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS the way a new flag NAME can - a deliberate env change to a service has to be re-frozen here, in the reviewed commit that makes it. `--set-env-vars` replaces the whole env set, so the value is edited in place rather than appended: dropping any of the four existing entries would silently unset them on the dashboard. Its position is load-bearing: the step can fail because the build service account lacks run.jobs.create, and placed anywhere earlier that failure would abort the build before the wheel/CC/dashboard revisions got their traffic — an ad-hoc measurement tool taking production deploys down with it. Behind the promotes it still fails the build loudly, but only after the services are out. THIRD DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase A): `deploy-backfill-job` is added to `step_ids` and `wait_for`, behind the same three promotes as `deploy-sweep-job` and for the same reason (a `run.jobs.create` failure must not strand a service deploy). The build now has TWO tail steps, so `test_sweep_job_runs_after_every_service_promote`'s `ids[-1] == 'deploy-sweep-job'` assertion was redesigned into `test_the_job_steps_are_the_tail_and_nothing_hides_behind_them`, which pins the tail as the SET `{deploy-sweep-job, deploy-backfill-job}` and re-checks each one's promote edges and marker-first script. Their order relative to each other is deliberately not asserted: they waitFor the same steps and Cloud Build runs them concurrently. NO pre-existing `waitFor` edge changed, and no deploy flag on any service changed. FOURTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase A): `deploy-bot-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET=options-wheel-chain-lake`. This is an ENV-STRING change to a pre-existing step, so — exactly like the SWEEP_JOB_NAME change above — it cannot be absorbed by ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS (that mechanism forgives a new flag NAME, never a changed VALUE) and is re-frozen here in the reviewed commit that makes it. Why the wheel service needs it: /regression's `lake_freshness` check reads CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET, and without it the check warns `lake_freshness_unconfigured` for ever - a detective control that looks alive and watches nothing. It must be in this literal list because --set-env-vars replaces the whole env set, so an out-of-band `services update` survives only until the next merge. The value is edited in place, appended to the existing three entries; dropping any of them would silently unset them on the wheel service. Deliberately NOT added to `deploy-cc-canary`: the covered-call profile has no stocks.symbols, so its copy of the check degrades to a `lake_freshness_no_universe` warn by design - the lake is the wheel's data and the wheel's check is its watcher. FIFTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase B PR-a): `compute-engine-identity` is added to `step_ids` (immediately before `build-dashboard-image`) and `build-dashboard-image`'s `waitFor` gains an edge on it — the only change to a pre-existing step's waitFor in this fixture's history, and it is re-frozen here rather than absorbed because `test_pre_existing_wait_for_edges_preserved` forgives no new edge but `serialize-builds`. Why the step exists: the sweep dedup key is now half `engine_identity` (the sha256 of the CONTENTS of `src/**`), and the dashboard image ships no `src/` tree to hash, so this step runs the SHARED module `src/backtesting/scenarios/engine_identity.py` against the checkout and hands the value to the dashboard build as an `ENGINE_IDENTITY` build-arg. It executes the FILE as `__main__` rather than importing the package (whose `__init__` drags in pandas and the Alpaca SDK), which is what lets it be a bare `python:3.11-slim` with no pip step; `waitFor: ['-']` keeps it off the critical path. `build-dashboard-image` becomes a `bash -c` step for the same reason — the build-arg's value has to be read out of /workspace — and it FAILS the build on an empty value rather than shipping a dashboard whose sweep dedup hint would be permanently disabled. No deploy flag on any service changed. SIXTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase B PR-c): the fourth canary chain. `deploy-sim-canary` / `smoke-test-sim` / `promote-sim` are added to `step_ids` and `wait_for`, positioned AFTER `promote-dashboard` and BEFORE the two Job deploys, and `deploy-sim-canary`'s full flag set is frozen here. Three things about it are new to this file and each is deliberate. (1) `--no-cpu-throttling`: the service returns 202 and continues the replay on a worker thread, and under Cloud Run's default request-based billing the CPU is throttled the moment that response returns — the background replay would starve, because nothing ever supplies an in-flight request (the console polls BigQuery through the dashboard and never touches this service). This is the plan's rev-3 blocker fix and it is pinned here so it cannot be dropped as a cost saving. (2) `--concurrency=1`: the engine mutates process-global state during a replay, so two replays in one process would corrupt each other's numbers without crashing. The service refuses a second request itself; this flag is what stops one queueing invisibly behind the first. (3) `--set-secrets` appears on a SERVICE deploy for the first time, and the wheel/CC steps' comments say not to do that. Their reason is that those services were provisioned by hand and their bindings persist; `sim-service` does not exist yet and THIS STEP CREATES IT, so a first deploy without the bindings produces a service whose `Config()` cannot validate — it fails at startup and the build goes red for a reason no log explains. The names are `deploy-sweep-job`'s, verbatim. Also re-frozen: `deploy-dashboard-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `SIM_SERVICE_URL`. That is an ENV-STRING change to a pre-existing step, so — exactly like SWEEP_JOB_NAME and CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET before it — it cannot be absorbed by ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS (that mechanism forgives a new flag NAME, never a changed VALUE) and is re-frozen in the reviewed commit that makes it. The proxy `POST /api/v2/sims/run` fails closed with a 503 naming this variable when it is absent, rather than defaulting to a URL that might not exist. `timeout:` is UNCHANGED at 1500s; the redone budget (~975s single, ~1335s waiting-pair) is in cloudbuild.yaml's own comment with the >1000s escalation rule. No pre-existing `waitFor` edge changed and no other service's deploy flags changed. SEVENTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase B PR-c follow-up): `create-sim-service-if-absent` is added to `step_ids` (immediately before `deploy-sim-canary`) and `deploy-sim-canary`'s `waitFor` gains an edge on it — the second time a pre-existing step's waitFor is re-frozen rather than absorbed, because `test_pre_existing_wait_for_edges_preserved` forgives no new edge but `serialize-builds`. Why the step exists: `gcloud run deploy --no-traffic` is REJECTED when the service does not exist ("--no-traffic not supported when creating a new service"), and that killed build `2e1b180`'s deploy. The three older chains never met it because their services were provisioned by hand long before their steps existed; `sim-service` is the first service this repo creates from cloudbuild. The creation is a SEPARATE step rather than a branch inside the canary deploy specifically so that `deploy-sim-canary`'s frozen flag set stays byte-identical: `--no-traffic` and `--tag=canary` are the flags that MAKE it a canary, and putting them behind a shell variable so creation could omit them would have required deleting them from this freeze — which is the one thing stopping a canary from quietly becoming a live deploy. The bootstrap revision takes no `--revision-suffix` and no `--tag` (it must not collide with the canary revision, and the smoke reads the canary-tagged URL), so a first build produces two revisions and `promote-sim` — UNCHANGED, and deliberately not branching on the marker the step writes — moves traffic to the canary. Every later build is a single `describe` and a no-op. NO deploy flag on any service changed. EIGHTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase B PR-d): `deploy-backfill-job`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `BACKFILL_THEN_BATTERY=true`. NOTE the shape of this one: the Job steps are NOT in `deploy_flags` (that block freezes the four SERVICE canaries), so no frozen VALUE in this file changes and nothing here had to be regenerated — the env is pinned instead by `test_the_backfill_job_composes_the_weekly_battery` in tests/test_cloudbuild_contract.py, alongside the other per-Job env assertions that have always lived there. It is recorded in this note anyway because it is a deliberate deploy-behaviour change to a pre-existing step and the same review rule applies: `--set-env-vars` replaces the whole env set, so it is edited in place and dropping any of the four existing entries would silently unset them on the Job. What it does: after a SUCCESSFUL backfill the same execution runs `--command battery`, which re-measures the standing set and every active pin against the lake it just refreshed. A FAILED backfill skips it and keeps its own non-zero exit (the Job-failure policy pages); the battery always exits 0 and reports its own failures as a `battery_degraded` ERROR log watched by a 24h nag policy. The `backfill-weekly` scheduler is unchanged, which is why the flag is on the Job definition rather than on the schedule. `--task-timeout` is UNCHANGED at 21600s and `main.BATTERY_MAX_SECONDS` (14400) is pinned strictly inside it by `test_the_battery_wall_cap_fits_inside_the_backfill_jobs_timeout`. No step id, no `waitFor` edge, no service deploy flag and no `timeout:` changed. ELEVENTH DEVIATION (FC-096 Phase D PR-1): `deploy-dashboard-canary`'s `--set-env-vars` gains `IAP_AUDIENCE=/projects/799970961417/locations/us-central1/services/options-wheel-dashboard` and `OPERATORS=zeshan@tkzmgroup.com`. Same mechanism as the SWEEP_JOB_NAME and CHAIN_LAKE_BUCKET deviations above: an env VALUE is part of the frozen flag string, so ALLOWED_NEW_DEPLOY_FLAGS (which forgives a new flag NAME) cannot absorb it, and the change is re-frozen here in the reviewed commit that makes it. Both entries are appended in place; `--set-env-vars` replaces the whole env set, so dropping any of the six existing entries would silently unset them on the dashboard. IAP_AUDIENCE is the exact `aud` that direct-Cloud-Run IAP stamps on assertions for THIS service - leading slash, project NUMBER, deliberately not derived from $PROJECT_ID (which is the project *id*) because a wrong-but-plausible audience fails closed silently. OPERATORS is SPACE-separated on purpose: a comma is this flag's own variable separator, so the day a second operator is added a comma-joined value would silently become a second env var. ACKNOWLEDGED, on the record (plan rev 3, PR-1 bullet): this puts the operator's email address in a public repository, here and in cloudbuild.yaml. It is already public in commit authorship and in docs/; an allowlist is an authorization list rather than a secret (possessing it grants nothing without a Google session IAP admits); and the alternative - sourcing it from Secret Manager - would move the write allowlist out of the reviewed, version-controlled deploy config, which is exactly where a change to who may spend money should be visible. Also in this PR but NOT visible in this fixture: `dashboard/cloudbuild.yaml` is deleted. It was a stale second build config no trigger referenced (the only trigger, deploy-options-wheel-strategy, uses the root file), carrying `--allow-unauthenticated` and a TRADING_BOT_URL in a different project - a footgun to have lying around during exactly this work.
